chapters.reason: The paper introduces a novel training strategy that randomly mixes latent and text tokens to enable fast adaptation to new latent tokens, which aligns with the description of specialized training strategies for models with recurrent activation flows, such as curriculum-based compression and CoT-aligned supervision.

The paper fine-tunes LLMs on hybrid data with an extended vocabulary, aiming to unlock latent reasoning capabilities through specialized training without explicit architectural modifications, fitting the description of training-induced recurrence.

The paper addresses reducing reasoning trace length via latent tokens, indirectly relating to layer depth as a bottleneck for reasoning capacity, as shorter latent traces may alleviate depth constraints for multi-step reasoning.
